## Hands-on 1 – The reproduction {#hands-on-1-the-reproduction .smaller}

::: {.small}
**Task 3 in the browser lab.** Choose one of two analysts, run their cells in order, and reach the value on record. Every cell with gaps to fill has a hint and a full solution beneath it.

| Analyst | Data | Model | Recorded by Multi100 |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| C6HJR | the course panel, 270 country-years | fixed effects for country and year, conventional standard errors | t = −3.804 on 233 df |
| KQXUE | `analyst_KQXUE.csv`, 270 country-years rebuilt from the code of the analyst | a fixed effect for each country, conventional standard errors | t = −7.169 on 242 df |
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
When you have your value, write the analyst and the *t*, for example `KQXUE t = -7.169`, hold it, and send it when I say go. If you finish early, take the other analyst.
:::

::: notes
Now you work, on the question at the heart of reproducibility: given the data and the model, does the recorded number come back? Open Task 3 in the browser lab and choose one of two analysts. Mine runs on the course panel, with fixed effects for country and year. KQXUE built a panel of its own, which the course rebuilt from the Stata code that the analyst deposited, and gave each country a fixed effect and no year effects. Each analyst has a few cells, one step to a cell, and every gap has a hint and a solution underneath; using them is not cheating. The page offers a third analyst, whose first cell downloads two large packages; leave that one for later. When you have your value, write the analyst and the t, hold it, and send it when I say go. [circulate; then go]
:::
